ASEAN's reliance on Middle Eastern crude oil, coupled with rising global prices, has prompted discussions on implementing regional fuel-security measures and long-term initiatives like the ASEAN Power Grid and renewable energy deployment

items: Southeast Asian energy ministers are meeting in Manila to address vulnerabilities in energy security due to the ongoing Middle East conflict, which has heightened concerns over imported energy prices and supply disruptions.

Analysts emphasize the need for structural changes to reduce dependence on imported fuels, with projections indicating a significant increase in Southeast Asia's energy import bill by 2035 without such changes.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Southeast Asian energy ministers meeting in Manila this week face the prospect of a prolonged Middle East war that has exposed the region’s vulnerabilities to imported energy.

As the US-Israeli war against Iran drags on, there is increased urgency for ASEAN to implement its proposed energy security plans and reduce its exposure to price shocks caused by attacks on infrastructure and shipping routes in the Middle East.

ASEAN imports more than half of the crude for its refineries from the Middle East at a time when global benchmark prices are around $100 a barrel. The conflict has also sharpened concerns about broader energy security risks as Chinese refiners have suspended oil product exports for October.

blocks.caption: Gasoline, kerosene prices rise on October 6, diesel gets slight rollback

blocks.text: Against that backdrop, energy ministers meeting in Manila are expected to review regional fuel-security measures launched after emergency talks earlier this year, including efforts to put into effect coordinated emergency responses under the ASEAN Framework Agreement on Petroleum Security (APSA).
Long-term initiatives, including the ASEAN Power Grid and renewable-energy deployment, are also on the agenda.

“What the crisis brought was a sharper focus on resiliency,” Philippine Energy Undersecretary Felix Fuentebella told Reuters on October 1, saying energy security had moved from a technical issue to a priority for ASEAN ministers and leaders.
The higher prices are raising costs for the region’s households and eating into the earnings of transport workers.

“We hardly take anything home anymore,” said Antonio Bandin, a Manila jeepney driver who joined a protest last week over rising fuel prices. His working fuel bill has more than doubled to about P2,400 per day.

The ASEAN Centre for Energy warned in a policy paper that a severe disruption to Middle East supplies could place oil volumes equivalent to nearly 28% of ASEAN’s final oil consumption at risk, underscoring the need for stronger regional petroleum-security arrangements.

But the region’s insufficient storage capacity and inventories remain obstacles to implementing APSA, Alloysius Joko Purwanto, senior energy economist at the Economic Research Institute for ASEAN and East Asia, warned on Friday during a webinar hosted by the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
Energy Secretary Sharon Garin has said the Philippines, which remains under a national energy emergency, is exploring regional fuel-stockpiling arrangements and could host future storage projects.
But analysts cautioned that such measures are unlikely to affect the present crisis.

“This is more about preparing for the next crisis. A reserve is a buffer. It is not a strategy,” Christopher Len, a senior fellow at the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute, said in the same webinar, referring to regional stockpiling initiatives.
Ministers are also expected to discuss ways to reduce long-term dependence on imported fuels. Renewable energy, electric vehicles, and energy efficiency are expected to feature prominently.
The International Energy Agency estimates Southeast Asia’s energy import bill could rise from more than $80 billion in 2024 to about $245 billion by 2035 without structural change.

The IEA said wider electrification, including electric vehicles and biofuels, would help curb oil demand and reduce exposure to volatile fuel imports, while cross-border links under the ASEAN Power Grid that would integrate the region’s electrical network will require about $27 billion in investment by 2040.
“We should actually use this shock as a lesson to reduce exposure, not only to cushion it,” Len said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Oil from South Korea being shipped to Russia as Ukraine war grinds on
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Guardian analysis finds more than 150,000 tonnes of fuel was shipped to Russian ports in July and August, some using sanctioned tankers

Oil is being shipped from South Korea to…

blocks.text: Oil is being shipped from South Korea to Russia via sanctioned tankers as Moscow scrambles for supplies amid the war in Ukraine, a move one expert said “undermines” Seoul’s public backing for Kyiv.

Guardian analysis of port records and ship-tracking data found that in July and August over 176,000 tonnes of fuel, mostly diesel, was loaded at several South Korean ports on to seven tankers that made 14 voyages to Russia’s far east.

Three of the vessels were under sanctions by the UK and EU, and one took on its cargo through a ship-to-ship transfer in South Korean waters – a method that can obscure where a cargo came from and lets ships avoid calling at port terminals.

“It is shocking that EU-sanctioned tankers loaded fuel at South Korean ports and carried it to Russia”, said Isaac Levi, an analyst at the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), a Finnish thinktank. “This undermines the sanctions regime and South Korea’s support for Ukraine.”
Seoul has sent Ukraine humanitarian aid and non-lethal military supplies such as helmets, body armour and demining vehicles, and in 2023 pledged $2.3bn in support, most of it in loans.

But South Korea has long sought to balance its support for Ukraine with its desire to improve ties with Russia. Throughout the war, Seoul has ruled out sending weapons directly to Ukraine, in line with its practice of not supplying lethal arms to countries at war. Moscow has signalled an interest in restoring relations with South Korea, including trade ties.

While the fuel trade involves vessels sanctioned by some of Seoul’s western partners, it does not appear to breach South Korean law. South Korea’s own measures against Russia rely mainly on export controls on goods such as industrial machinery, electronics and vehicles.

The shipments, however, risk making Seoul look like a weak link in western efforts to pressure Russia, as relations with Kyiv come under strain over the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea, which Seoul says was meant to remain secret.
It is unclear who owned or sold the fuel, which South Korean port records do not show.

The largest carrier, the sanctioned Layla, made two voyages from the south-eastern port of Ulsan to Vladivostok leaving on 19 July and 10 August and carrying 57,000 tonnes of diesel in total. On the first trip, it told South Korean authorities its destination was Vladivostok, but on the second it said it was bound for Niigata in Japan.

Another sanctioned tanker, the Russian-flagged Astoria, which is also under Australian sanctions, loaded nearly 11,000 tonnes of fuel at Ulsan on 1 August, declaring Japan as its destination, before sailing to Vladivostok.

The third sanctioned tanker, the Chongchon, never berthed. It took on about 26,000 tonnes of fuel from an unsanctioned tanker, the Celeste I, at an anchorage off the southern South Korean port of Yeosu in early August, then headed to Vladivostok after declaring Singapore as its destination.
The owners and managers of the four tankers did not respond to requests for comment.

Russia’s capacity to refine oil has been severely disrupted by Ukrainian drone strikes. Its refinery throughput fell in June to its lowest level in more than 20 years, and diesel output is down nearly 30% on last year, according to the International Energy Agency.
Ukraine’s military intelligence agency, the HUR, says Moscow has been forced to import fuel products to feed the “Russian war machine”.

According to data from the maritime analytics firm Kpler, the buyers included Rosneft, Russia’s state-controlled oil company, which is under UK, US, EU and Australian sanctions, and NNK, a Russian oil group whose owner, Eduard Khudainatov, and one of its companies, NNK-Oil, are under UK sanctions.

In August, Russia imported 368,000 tonnes of oil products by sea, more than seven times the previous month and the highest monthly total since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, according to Kpler data analysed by CREA. South Korea accounted for 112,000 tonnes, or 31%, of that amount, second only to India.
Loadings at South Korean ports began to surge in July, just as the country’s president, Lee Jae Myung, pledged $100m for Ukraine’s reconstruction at a Nato summit in Turkey.
A 2025 trade association survey found that nearly 80% of South Korean firms that had stopped exporting to Russia since the war began were open to resuming trade.
In March, as the war with Iran shut the strait of Hormuz, South Korea capped exports of certain fuels and imported Russian naphtha under a US sanctions waiver.
On 1 October, the UK temporarily exempted South Korea’s existing gas contracts from a ban on maritime services for Russian LNG that takes effect in January 2027.

When contacted, South Korea’s foreign ministry did not address the shipments or the sanctioned tankers. In a statement, it said that as “a responsible member of the international community, the government supports, and is actively taking part in, international efforts to help end the war in Ukraine and bring about a peaceful recovery.”

It said it had expanded its export controls on Russia under the Foreign Trade Act “beyond strategic items to 1,402 non-strategic items with a high potential for diversion to military use” and was “strictly enforcing” them.
The government “continues to monitor the implementation of its export controls on Russia and, where necessary, takes action in accordance with the relevant laws and regulations,” the ministry said.
The UK Foreign Office did not answer questions about the UK-sanctioned tankers using South Korean ports, or say whether the shipments had been raised with Seoul.

A spokesperson said: “The UK remains firmly committed to the effective monitoring of our sanctions and to working with international partners to increase economic pressure on Russia and reduce the revenues funding its illegal war against Ukraine.”

articles.title: NDRRMC: State of calamity declared in 106 areas due to El Niño
articles.summary: State of calamity was declared in 106 areas as dry conditions driven by the El Niño phenomenon continue to intensify across the country.

blocks.text: Published October 6, 2026 7:25am
State of calamity was declared in 106 areas as dry conditions driven by the El Niño phenomenon continue to intensify across the country.
In its report on Monday, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) said these areas are in five regions:

items: Cagayan Valley - 66
Calabarzon - 4
Bicol - 12
Soccsksargen - 1
Caraga - 23

blocks.text: At least 39 wild, forest, and mountain fire incidents were recorded in Caraga Administrative Region.
Four cities and municipalities reported water supply interruptions, while 33 localities were forced to suspend classes in the region.
Across the country, the NDRRMC reported that 104,149 families or 388,375 individuals have been affected by El Niño, particularly in Cagayan Valley, Bicol, Calabarzon, and Caraga.
Agricultural damage and production losses were estimated at P5.56 billion, according to the NDRRMC. Cagayan Valley accounted for the majority of agricultural destruction with P4.96 billion.
A total of 201,322 farmers and fisherfolk have been affected nationwide, with over 223,497 hectares of crop areas damaged.
Of the total affected farmland, 41,164 hectares suffered total crop loss with no chance of recovery.
Assistance worth P39,058,681 has been provided to affected communities so far, according to the NDRRMC.
On June 9, state weather bureau PAGASA said that indicators confirmed that El Niño conditions were present in the tropical Pacific.
In May 2026, the observed relative sea surface temperature anomaly indicated a warming trend consistent with El Niño development.
El Niño increases the likelihood of below-normal rainfall conditions, which may result in adverse impacts such as dry spells and droughts in some areas of the country.
However, over the western part of the country, above-normal rainfall conditions during the Southwest monsoon season may also occur.
On September 23, PAGASA warned of a possibly record-breaking El Niño in the coming months.
Lesser rains are to be expected come October due to the El Niño phenomenon, the state weather bureau said.

PAGASA also said that the El Niño could last until March or even June. Around 40 provinces are expected to experience lesser rainfall during the dry spell and drought. Once January comes, it is expected that this number could leap to 80. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: ‘A God-almighty punch-up’: rare footage shows Battle of Hastings (the 1966 one)
articles.summary:
English Heritage acquires film of first re-enactment, ‘a lot of pushing and shoving’ between Kent and Sussex students

At the top of a hill in a field near Hastings, a group of defiant…

blocks.text: At the top of a hill in a field near Hastings, a group of defiant English combatants awaited the invading army of William the Conqueror, brandishing their spears and shouting “Harold! Harold!”.

Unfortunately, the Norman army had been held up in traffic on the A27 from Brighton, meaning the most significant battle in English history had to be delayed by 20 minutes while the French got into their costumes.

On 14 October 1966, when a group of 500 students from Kent and Sussex universities met to re-enact the Battle of Hastings to mark its 900th anniversary, not every aspect was strictly historically accurate. Yes, the event was being staged on the same fields outside Battle in East Sussex where the original clash happened, but the English were wearing belted sacks and their swords and axes were made of wood and hardboard that had been painted silver.

blocks.caption: ‘A pleasingly Monty Pythonesque record’: university students in combat at the first Battle of Hastings re-enactment in October 1966.  Photograph: Keystone Press/Alamy

blocks.text: The rivalry between Kent and Sussex universities was real enough, however, according to Peter Sampson, a Sussex fresher who had been persuaded to sign up by the prospect of “a grand day out” and the promise of free beer. Once the two sides met, he says, it turned into “a God-almighty punch-up”.

“There was actually a lot of real pushing and shoving, a lot of fighting going on in there … My friend John got a big whack around the head with the end of a [fake] spear, which hurt his face quite a lot.”

Sixty years after that first re-enactment spawned an annual event which still attracts thousands of visitors each year, English Heritage has acquired rare colour footage of the inaugural event, at which a bemused French foreign minister attended, Queen Matilda was played by Miss World and health and safety was a far-off dream.

blocks.caption: Chaps in fake chainmail bonking each other on the heads with fake weapons: Battle of Hastings re-enactors in 1966.  Photograph: Keystone Press/Alamy

blocks.text: It was filmed by Alan Wootton, an innovative manufacturer of electronics who lived in Hastings and had been invited to capture a film record of the celebrations by Hastings town council. The film came to light when Alan’s son Cliff, who had helped out on the day as a 12-year-old, recently visited Battle Abbey, the medieval foundation that was built on the site of the skirmish and is today overseen by English Heritage. He mentioned to a volunteer that he had 300 reels of film of the event, and would the charity be interested in seeing them?

The result – condensed into a 12-minute film – is a pleasingly Monty Pythonesque record of chaps in fake chainmail bonking each other on the heads with fake weapons while others ride around a bit on horses and 30,000 highly partisan (ie anti-French) spectators look on. (Though the era-defining British comedy, pedants will note, did not air until three years later.)
“When Cliff showed me the footage, I was blown away by it, it was really, really impressive,” says James Witcombe, the site manager of Battle Abbey.

blocks.caption: Re-enactors marking the 950th anniversary of the Battle of Hastings in October 2016. Photograph: Jack Taylor/Getty Images

blocks.text: The film is, he says, very much of its time – and very different from the event which the charity has continued to stage every year since. “Looking at it from a modern perspective – yeah, it is a little bit of an interesting watch. I think the thing that’s very obvious is that it’s a load of amateurs getting together and really having fun … From our point of view, that’s the atmosphere that we want to preserve, just making sure we’ve got a few more sort of boundaries in place and nobody actually gets hurt.”

Present-day crowds still tend to back “the home side”, he says, though “it’s a bit less partisan than it used to be”. This year’s event will be staged on 10 and 11 October, with a full battle run-through each day (though the result, sadly for England fans, does not change).

blocks.caption: ‘It’s a bit less partisan than it used to be: thousands of visitors now attend the annual event (October 2018 pictured).  Photograph: Jonny Weeks/The Guardian

blocks.text: Today’s re-enactors – 1,000 combatants are expected this year – pay rather more attention to historical details, says Witcombe. “Whereas in 1966, there were knitted outfits and all that sort of stuff, the re-enactors today take it very seriously. It’s all about authenticity and, actually, experimental archaeology – [the idea that] living the experience gives you a much greater insight.” With the Bayeux tapestry’s presence in London having driven up interest in all things Norman, English Heritage is expecting bumper crowds – and is inviting any of those involved in the original 1966 event to come along.

As Sampson recalls, while the battlefield itself was certainly “edgy”, once hostilities ended after 25 minutes of fisticuffs, things became much more convivial. After the promised free beer did not materialise, “we took matters somewhat into our own hands and, shall we say, liberated a couple of beer kegs from the back of the refreshment tent.
“We cracked them open and then sat down with the Kent lads and lasses, and in the warm afternoon sunshine, just discussed the events of the day. So it became very friendly at the end of the day.”

articles.title: The secret to the Lopez family’s enduring control of ABS-CBN
articles.summary: Why are the Lopezes still calling the shots at ABS-CBN even as an outsider pays most of its rescue?

blocks.text: A company that did not exist until February 2026 is about to become the largest single shareholder of ABS-CBN Corp.’s listed shares. However, the founding Lopez family will still decide how the network is run.

On Wednesday, September 30, ABS-CBN’s stockholders gathered virtually to approve the changes that make room for the P6-billion equity rescue package. To make room for that capital, stockholders approved a tripling of authorized capital and cleared the way for ABS-CBN to issue 1.64 billion new common shares at P3.65 each to five separate subscribers. More than half of that money—P3.5 billion—will come from a fresh outside investor, I&C Holdings Corporation, which will become the single largest common shareholder with 958.9 million shares, or 37.7% of the total common stock. (READ: ABS-CBN talks up its ‘new’ future, but its new owners weren’t in the room)
Meanwhile, the family’s longtime parent holding firm, Lopez Inc., will see its direct economic slice of common shares compressed from 55.82% down to roughly 23%.

By standard public market logic, an outside investor with 37.7% of the ordinary shares would expect a real say in the boardroom, while a founding family whose holding vehicle fell under 25% would lose control.
Except that didn’t happen because ABS-CBN’s common shares tell only half the story.

During the special stockholders meeting, ABS-CBN chairman Martin L. Lopez was asked who will call the shots now that there is outsider’s money. His answer: “Lopez Inc. together with its stockholders, Crème, Mantes and Presta, and together with ABS-CBN will continue to determine ABS-CBN’s strategic direction. The new major investor will be consulted and their rights will be respected.”
So the savior, who is an outsider with P3.5 billion, will merely be consulted. But the steering wheel stays inside the family.

How can a family retain almost absolute command over a public company while owning a minority of its listed shares? The secret is a financial fortress built more than a decade ago: unlisted, low-par voting preferred shares. And as the latest regulatory filings reveal, the Lopezes didn’t just preserve that fortress on September 30. They expanded it with a brand new 300-million-share buffer.
The system that protects ABS-CBN from corporate raiders, outside accumulators, and public minority revolts rests on having two different kinds of shares.

Most listed companies operate under the principle of “one share, one vote” using ordinary common shares. ABS-CBN has those too. What sets these apart is that ABS-CBN’s shares do not all cost the same. These common shares have a face value of P1 each, and are listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) under the ticker ABS.
But sitting alongside them is a second class of stock: one billion voting preferred shares.
These preferred shares carry three crucial characteristics:

items: Full voting rights: Each preferred share carries one full vote, identical in voting weight as one P1 common share.

A 20-centavo par value: Each preferred share has a par value of only P0.20, one-fifth the P1 par value of a common share. More importantly, when ABS-CBN issued the preferred shares in 2013, they were issued at par.

Unlisted: Unlike ABS-CBN’s common shares, the preferred shares cannot be bought on the stock exchange. They cannot be traded, snapped up on market dips, or accumulated by hostile parties through stockbrokers. And ABS-CBN holds the right of first refusal before any sale to an outsider.

blocks.text: This is where the math gets interesting. Back in 2013, ABS-CBN actually offered the billion preferred shares to its existing Filipino shareholders at 20 centavos each, with Lopez Inc. committing to buy whatever the others did not. Lopez Inc. ended up with 987,130,246 of them, or 98.71% of the preferred class. The total cash spent by the family was roughly P197.4 million.

In exchange for that modest sum, Lopez Inc. captured nearly one billion uncontested votes. ABS-CBN itself disclosed that the preferred-share subscription increased Lopez Inc.’s voting interest in the company to 79%.

Think about what happened: P197.4 million in preferred shares gave Lopez Inc. nearly one billion votes. A common share had a P1 par value and one vote. A preferred share had a par value of just 20 centavos — but it also had one vote.
Put simply: The same amount of money could buy 5x as many votes through preferred shares than through common shares.

In Philippine corporate law, a shareholder’s voting power is measured against all outstanding voting shares, not just the total of common shares that trade. Because of these preferred shares, the total number of votes in ABS-CBN’s boardroom grew much larger than what is traded on the stock exchange. Before the P6-billion rescue deal, the company had 899.85 million regular common shares and one billion preferred shares, creating a total voting pool of 1.9 billion shares. Lopez Inc. owned around 502.3 million common shares (around 55.8% of common) on top of its 987.13 million preferred shares.
That gave Lopez Inc. its superpower: 78.4% total voting power.

That gap meant the public shareholders, even voting together, could never outvote the Lopez Inc. block. When Batangas lawmaker Leandro Leviste accumulated 90 million shares in 2024 to build a 10% common stake, he was celebrated as the network’s second-largest owner. But when measured against all voting shares in the room, his 90 million common shares gave him just 4.74% of the vote. He held no veto power, no swing vote, and not enough votes to guarantee even one board seat under cumulative voting. The 20-centavo preferred shares acted as an unbreachable wall.

blocks.caption: Leandro Leviste’s ABS-CBN stake is shrinking, and so is everyone else’s

blocks.text: The crisis that forced ABS-CBN to seek P6 billion in rescue funds was, among others, heavy debt. After losing its broadcast franchise in 2020, the company racked up over P45 billion in total losses. By the end of 2025, the lenders’ promise not to call a default over the lost franchise had run its course, and ABS-CBN’s P8.5 billion in bank loans, mostly owed to BPI and UnionBank, had all come due within a year. (READ: Why ABS-CBN is still retrenching 200 employees with P6 billion on the way)

At the same time, the Lopez family conglomerate fractured. The clean energy and utilities side of the business group led by Federico “Piki” Lopez ring-fenced First Gen and First Philippine Holdings, refusing to drain cash reserves to prop up struggling ABS-CBN’s debt. His camp declined to put in P2 billion, and has said audit findings had to be resolved first.

The stalemate finally broke in August 2026 when former ABS-CBN chairman Eugenio “Gabby” Lopez III sold his family branch’s 25.68% stake in top parent Lopez Inc. to Ramon S. Ang for P11.6 billion. (READ: [Rappler’s Best] The day Gabby Lopez said, ‘We’re done’)

blocks.caption: Ramon Ang buys his way into Lopez Inc., which owns what he already builds

blocks.text: That private windfall bypassed the old corporate hierarchy. Instead of coursing funds through Lopez Inc., three individual Lopez family branches, using their “personal resources”, signed up to buy ABS-CBN primary common shares in their own names:

items: Crème Investment Corp. (Geny Lopez branch): P766.7 million (210.0 million shares).
Mantes Corporation (Manuel Lopez branch): P766.7 million (210.0 million shares).
Presta Holdings Company (Presentacion Lopez-Psinakis branch): P666.7 million (182.6 million shares).

blocks.text: Combined with a modest P300 million subscription from Lopez Inc. itself, the family committed to put in P2.5 billion in new equity. Alongside them sat I&C Holdings, providing P3.5 billion. I&C paid a P1.5 billion deposit at signing and owes the P2 billion balance after the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approves the new structure. Lopez Inc. paid its P300 million in full. (READ: Family friend to referee? SEC’s Francis Lim has peace plan for Lopez war.)

Because 1.64 billion new common shares flooded into existence, the total common pool expanded from 899.8 million to 2.54 billion shares. Lopez Inc.’s direct common stake dropped from about 55.8% down to 22.98%. On common shares alone, Lopez Inc. lost its absolute majority.
Yet when the voting preferred shares were factored into the new 3.54 billion voting denominator, the family’s control remained ironclad:
Even without counting I&C, the four Lopez vehicles together command 61.37% of the total vote. And when allied with I&C’s 27.06%, the insider coalition locks up an overwhelming 88.43% supermajority.
What the bloc will not have is two-thirds. Any charter amendment or new capital increase will need votes from I&C or the minority shareholders.
The public float was squeezed down from 16.75% to 8.98%. Leviste’s voting voice was cut nearly in half to 2.54%. The insiders rearranged the chairs, and the outsiders absorbed the dilution.
A 61.37% majority settles today’s votes. What ABS-CBN’s board did three weeks before the September 30 meeting bears on tomorrow’s.

On August 19, 2026, the ABS-CBN board initially approved expanding its Authorized Capital Stock from P1.5 billion to P4.5 billion. Under that first plan, common shares were set to jump to 4.30 billion (at P1 par), while preferred shares stayed capped at their old one billion limit (at P0.20 par).
Under that structure, every single preferred share authorized by the company was already issued and nearly all of them owned by Lopez Inc. There was zero preferred headroom left.

On September 8, just three weeks before the stockholders met to vote, the board met again to change its plan. Total authorized capital remained unchanged at P4.5 billion, but the underlying share counts were reallocated:

items: Authorized common shares were cut by 60 million (lowered from 4.30 billion to 4.24 billion).
Authorized preferred shares were raised by 300 million (raised from 1.0 billion to 1.30 billion).

blocks.text: The peso matched perfectly: 60 million common shares at P1.00 par equals P60 million. And 300 million preferred shares at P0.20 par equals exactly P60 million.
So why create 300 million new preferred shares when all P6 billion worth of incoming subscriptions consisted entirely of common shares?
It points to an on-demand corporate defense mechanism: a reserve of cheap votes that can be issued if the family’s majority is ever threatened.

After this deal closes, ABS-CBN will have 2.54 billion common shares issued, leaving roughly 1.7 billion unissued common shares in reserve. If ABS-CBN ever needs to issue hundreds of millions of additional common shares in future fund-raising, mergers, or debt payoffs, the family’s 61.37% voting margin would steadily drop.

By creating 300 million unissued preferred shares, the board created an emergency voting pool. And because preferred shares carry full voting rights at just 20 centavos each, the family can buy that entire 300-million pool in the future for just P60 million in cash. For an amount that costs less than producing a single prime-time television drama, the family can instantly generate 300 million brand-new votes to restore their majority whenever their control is threatened.

blocks.caption: Who writes the Lopez story? How lawyers, headlines, and ABS-CBN shape a family war

blocks.text: On September 30, stockholders approved the entire plan.

Tripling capital stock and changing corporate articles requires the approval of at least two-thirds, or 66.7%, of all outstanding voting shares under Philippine corporate law. For companies owned by thousands of scattered public shareholders —ABS-CBN had 5,138 stockholders of record at end-2025— gathering 66.7% of the votes is a massive hurdle.
For the Lopezes, it was a breeze.

Between Lopez Inc.’s 987.1 million preferred shares and the family’s common stock, the bloc walked into the virtual meeting with 1,576,374,534 shares present or represented—commanding 82.97% of the total vote.

When the corporate secretary read the resolution to amend Article Sixth (expanding the board from 7 to 9 seats) and Article Seventh (tripling authorized capital and creating the 300-million preferred buffer), the results were decisive: 1.58 billion shares voted FOR (82.97%); zero shares voted AGAINST, and 1,606 shares ABSTAINED.
No one voted against, and no one asked about the 300 million preferred shares.

The meeting did not address takeovers, and after the deal the family loses two-thirds. Leandro Leviste’s 90 million shares, whether voted by proxy or left uncast, were mathematically powerless against an 83% voting block.

I&C Holdings will secure its 37.7% economic slice. Two internal broadcast executives—ABS-CBN COO and head of creative programs Ma. Socorro “Cory” Vidanes and chief partnership officer Roberto “Bobot” Barreiro — were elected to the two board seats. And Carlo Katigbak’s management team was confirmed to remain intact. (READ: Inside Piki Lopez’s town hall as cousins rally for ABS-CBN)

Public investors who buy ABS-CBN shares on the open market might benefit if the studio’s turnaround succeeds and it starts making money again. But they do so strictly as passengers. By keeping voting power tied to 20-centavo preferred shares and carving out 300 million more for a rainy day, the Lopez family made sure that no matter how many outside billions arrive to save the company, the media company their fathers built will remain theirs. – Rappler.com

Lala Rimando wrote about Philippine business, and managed newsrooms, including Newsbreak, ABS-CBN, Rappler, and Forbes, for over 25 years. She’s now based in La Union, taking care of her mom with dementia, and working on the multimedia biography of the late John Gokongwei.

articles.title: Former American Idol contestant Caleb Flynn sentenced to life in prison for wife's murder
articles.summary: A former music pastor in Ohio who appeared briefly on American Idol was sentenced Monday to life in prison without the possibility of parole, after a jury convicted him last week of murdering his…

image.caption: Caleb Flynn is seen listening to a judge reading out a jury's verdict in an Ohio court on Sept. 29. The former American Idol contestant was sentenced Monday to life in prison without the possibility of parole, after a jury convicted him of murdering his wife while he was having an affair. (The Assoc

blocks.text: World·New

A former music pastor in Ohio who appeared briefly on American Idol was sentenced Monday to life in prison without the possibility of parole, after a jury convicted him last week of murdering his wife while he was having an affair.
Judge says Flynn showed no remorse for actions marked by 'deceit, manipulation and cruelty'
The judge said Caleb Flynn, 40, used his Christian faith to manipulate others and showed no remorse for actions marked by "layers of deceit, manipulation and cruelty."

With tears rolling down his cheeks, Flynn apologized to his family just before being sentenced, starting with his two young daughters, who were home when he shot his wife in her sleep. He called their births the "greatest joy in this life."
Although he said he accepted responsibility for his words and decisions, Flynn remained adamant that he was innocent.
"As I stand here before God, who is my ultimate judge, I am not lying when I say I did not kill my wife," he said.
Did not testify in own defence

Prosecutors said Flynn staged a home invasion in February and claimed a burglar killed his wife, Ashley Flynn, a 37-year-old schoolteacher and volleyball coach. In his 2013 appearance on American Idol, Flynn credited his wife with encouraging him to chase his dreams on the singing contest. He did not advance to the main competition in Hollywood.
During the trial, Flynn didn't testify on his own behalf, nor did anybody else.
Family members, including Ashley's parents, spoke in favour of the harsh sentence Monday, while saying they had forgiven Flynn because they didn't want her legacy to be hatred.

Her sister, Kayla Keyt, said Flynn's actions have scarred their entire church community, prompting children to run into their parents' bedrooms to make sure their fathers haven't killed their mothers.

As a family member read a statement written by his daughter Ava, Flynn sobbed uncontrollably as a pile of tissues grew on the defence table in front of him. At one point, it appeared he might fall over.

"Mommy was the perfect person," her statement said. "The absolute perfect person. What did she ever do to you to make you hate her so much?" In her statement, his daughter Alyssa said she wouldn't visit him in prison.
Wanted to leave marriage, jury told

During closing arguments, prosecutors told jurors that Flynn wanted out of his marriage when he shot his wife at their house in Tipp City, a suburb north of Dayton. He sent a text message to his lover the night before the shooting, saying, "I choose you. I'm free. Actions will come tomorrow," prosecutors said.

During the trial, Alleigha Botner testified she met Flynn in 2022 while she was a 20-year-old intern at his church and had an affair with him for more than a year. She told jurors that Flynn said he hated his wife and had thoughts of killing her.

The gun used to kill Ashley Flynn was not found at the scene, and his attorney told jurors that investigators found no evidence that Caleb Flynn fired a gun that day. Prosecutors said his fingerprints and DNA were at the scene and that his devices showed him moving around the house, even though he claimed he was asleep at the time of the shooting.
The jury found him guilty of multiple counts, including murder, felonious assault and tampering with evidence.

Of the amount, he said that P1.63 billion accounted for inflows, while P1.3 billion was for outflows. He also said there are P1.4 billion worth of covered and suspicious transactions with undetermined inflows and outflows.

articles.title: Trump approval ratings plummet to new low, polls show
articles.summary:
President says ‘I’m doing great’ despite polls showing 32% approval rating and loss of support from 2024 voters

Donald Trump’s approval ratings reached a record low on Monday, according to…

blocks.text: Donald Trump’s approval ratings reached a record low on Monday, according to new opinion polls.

A new Reuters/Ipsos poll shows Trump’s approval rating at a record-low 32%. That polling included the president losing support among independent voters and Latinos, who had backed him in 2024. The dip could prove dire for the Republican party a month ahead of the midterm elections that will determine control of Congress.
Before boarding a flight to Nebraska on Monday, Trump shrugged off questions about his approval ratings.
“I’m doing great,” Trump told a reporter, who’d asked about recent polls showing the president losing support among Latino voters, before blaming CNN and the media.

But according to a NBC News/Telemundo poll release Sunday, 59% of Latino voters prefer a Democratic-controlled Congress, double the number that supported the party two years ago. According to that poll, just 24% of Hispanic Americans approve of Trump’s performance.

Trump has spent the past few days campaigning across the country for Republican candidates, despite even conservative states starting to show the loss of support. Some Republicans have also started to distance themselves from the president over issues like immigration as they attempt to hold onto local support.
With Americans souring on the economy, the war with Iran, and other key issues they attribute to the administration, the impact of the negative sentiments could reach far and wide.

articles.title: This couple was swatted 55 times in 2 years over a post about Norm Macdonald
articles.summary: A Milwaukee couple was awarded a $575,000 US settlement from the city after armed police officers showed up at their homes 55 times in two years responding to bogus reports of violent crimes.

image.caption: Niki Robinson, left, and Patrick Tomlinson have been awarded a $575,000 US settlement by the City Milwaukee after armed police officers came to their home 55 times in two years responding to bogus reports of violent crime. (Submitted by Patrick Tomlinson)

blocks.text: As It Happens·New
A Milwaukee couple was awarded a $575,000 US settlement from the city after armed police officers showed up at their homes 55 times in two years responding to bogus reports of violent crimes.
Patrick Tomlinson and Niki Robinson awarded $575K US settlement from City of Milwaukee
The first time heavily armed police officers showed up at Patrick Tomlinson's house, he was asleep in bed, naked.
It was 1 a.m. on July 25, 2022, and someone had reported a hostage situation at his house in Milwaukee, where he lives with his wife, Niki Robinson.
"All of a sudden there's people pounding on the door," Tomlinson told As It Happens host Nil Kӧksal.
"I go outside to be pulled out of the house by eight or nine police officers [and] handcuffed on the front porch, which I can tell you is the least fun I've had handcuffed and naked in my life."

Tomlinson, a science fiction writer and comedian, hadn't committed a crime. He was the victim of "swatting," a harassment technique in which someone places a hoax call reporting a serious threat in order to send armed police to the target's home.

Over the course of the next two and a half years, Tomlinson and Robinson were swatted 55 times, despite repeatedly explaining their situation to the Milwaukee Police Department. They sued, and have been awarded a $575,000 US settlement from the City of Milwaukee.
LISTEN | Interview with 'swatting' victim Patrick Tomlinson:
As It Happens6:52This Milwaukee couple was swatted 55 times in 2 years
When asked for comment, Milwaukee police referred CBC to city attorney Evan Goyke, who did not respond to multiple requests for comment.

“While Niki and Patrick’s settlement provided closure and an acknowledgment of the violations of their rights, it is just as important that Milwaukee be more proactive looking forward," Jack Idlas, a lawyer for the couple, said in an emailed statement.

"The city has made no changes to policy and no officers have been disciplined for violating Niki and Patrick’s constitutional rights. That’s hard to believe after the taxpayers settled for over a half million dollars.
It started with a tweet
Tomlinson traces his troubles back to a social media post he made seven years ago about Canadian comedian Norm MacDonald.
In September 2018, he wrote on Twitter, now X: “Hot take: I’ve never found Norm Macdonald funny and was pretty sure all my comedy friends who did were either nuts or screwing with me."
After that, he says, he experienced years of online harassment, which is described in detail in an article in the Independent. That harassment, he says, eventually escalated into swatting.
"Our stalkers had specifically told us that they were going to begin swatting us…. We spoke to a dispatcher. We spoke with a desk sergeant. And both of them said there's nothing we can do," he said.
"Two weeks later, here I am, you know, on my front porch in the middle of the night, exposed to all my neighbours with shotguns and pistols and AR-15s pointed at my head."
Police were aware that Tomlinson's home was the target of swatting calls, according to internal memos and emails submitted as court evidence in the lawsuit.

On Aug. 3, 2022, one officer sent a memo to the acting police captain requesting the couple's home be marked as a "swatter house." The captain declined, saying it could cause a "complacency issue for responding officers.”
In bodycam footage from one incident, shared with CBC by Tomlinson's lawyers, an officer can be heard saying: "This guy keeps getting swatted."
Nevertheless, Tomlinson says, the police kept showing up, sometimes multiple times per day.

On one occasion, an officer entered his home without permission, according to an agreed statement of facts filed in connection with the lawsuit. On several occasions, officers searched the couple's home without a warrant.
Tomlinson says some of the officers responding to the hoax calls were "professional and sympathetic."
"Others, much less so," he said.

items: Trans Twitch star files human rights complaint against London, Ont., police after swatting arrest

blocks.text: It's been an exhausting ordeal for him and his wife, he said.

"Having each other there to support one another through this, emotionally and to know that we're not alone, without that, I don't think that either one of us individually would have been able to come out of this sane and intact," he said.
No charges or discipline
Nobody has been charged for the swatting calls, and none of the officers named in the lawsuit have been disciplined. The lawsuit settlement is not considered an admission of liability.

In his ruling, U.S. District Judge J.P. Stadtmueller determined that several police officers violated Tomlinson's and Robinson's constitutional rights by entering their home without permission and searching it without a warrant.

However, the judge granted those officers "qualified immunity," a legal doctrine that protects police and other government officials from prosecution or lawsuits for actions committed in the line of duty.
Most people don't realize that you don't have to be a celebrity or a politician to be targeted by this sort of thing.- Patrick Tomlinson, swatting victim
Tomlinson says he would like to see the officers involved disciplined, and for the police department to enact a detailed swatting policy.
In the meantime, he says, he and Robinson will keep speaking out.

"This is the only avenue, really, that we have to move the needle on this issue and to, you know, educate the public on this kind of harassment and stalking," he said. "Most people don't realize that you don't have to be a celebrity or a politician to be targeted by this sort of thing."
Interview with Patrick Tomlinson produced by Chris Trowbridge

articles.title: Tesla's exclusion from Manitoba EV program 'incredibly unfair,' politically motivated, court hears
articles.summary: Who in the Manitoba government decided to exclude Tesla from the province's electric vehicle rebate program, and why, is still unclear following a court hearing on the decision, the company's lawyers…

image.caption: A 2022 file photo shows a driver charging a Tesla electric vehicle. The company argues its exclusion from Manitoba's EV rebate program was unfair. (Paul Sancya/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Manitoba·New

Who in the Manitoba government decided to exclude Tesla from the province's electric vehicle rebate program, and why, is still unclear following a court hearing on the decision, the company's lawyers argue.
Decision made as part of budget, can't be reviewed by court, province argues

Who in the Manitoba government decided to exclude Tesla from the province's electric vehicle rebate program, and why, is still unclear following a court hearing on the decision, the company's lawyers argued in court Monday.

Lawyers for Tesla Motors Canada asked a Manitoba Court of King's Bench judge to overturn the NDP government's decision to exclude the company from electric vehicle rebates in the province in 2025 and 2026.
That move was unreasonable and unfair, and lacked transparency, the lawyers argued.
Manitoba's EV rebate program, which rolled out in 2024, entitled Manitobans to a $4,000 rebate on some new electric or hybrid plug-in vehicles, or $2,500 on used vehicles.
But in its spring 2025 budget, released just after the trade war began between the U.S. and Canada, the provincial government cut Tesla out of the rebate program. Chinese EVs were also excluded.

Manitoba's cut followed similar moves in B.C. and in Ontario, where Tesla won a 2018 legal case against the provincial government over its exclusion. Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island also announced Tesla exclusions from rebate programs the same month Manitoba did.

Tesla filed a judicial review application over the Manitoba exclusion earlier this year, naming the province, Manitoba Public Insurance and the ministers of finance, the environment and justice as respondents.
Manitoba budget targets Tesla, U.S. contractor in midst of trade war
The company argued its exclusion must be invalidated, since it's not clear which of the respondents made the decision or whether any of them were legally allowed to do so.
Michael Parrish, a lawyer for Tesla, called the province's decision to exclude Tesla "incredibly unfair."

A slim stack of documents provided by the province to show how it made the decision did not shed light on how a "still unidentified group of people" decided to exclude the company from the program, he told Justice Elissa Neville.
"What is at issue in this proceeding is the actual decision," he said. "We don't know why Tesla Canada was excluded, we don't know what information or documents were considered."

items: Tesla asks court to overturn exclusion from Manitoba EV rebate program

blocks.text: Tesla says it was not consulted before the exclusion and received no rationale from the province, aside from reading media reports that the decision was "made in order to be 'elbows up' in relation to the United States of America," the application says.

In court Monday, Parrish pointed to comments made by Premier Wab Kinew shortly after the company threatened legal action last May, in which the premier said Tesla CEO Elon Musk — a onetime ally of the U.S. president — should "get Donald Trump to stop the tariffs, and then we can talk about the EV rebate."
Based on those comments, Parrish argued that Tesla Canada was excluded from the EV rebate for "seemingly political reasons."
Tesla also argued the exclusion runs counter to the rebate program's objectives of making EVs more affordable for Manitobans.
'Budgetary decision': province
Joseph Langan, a lawyer for the Manitoba government, said the decision to exclude Tesla was made as part of the provincial budget and is therefore unreviewable by the courts.
"This doesn't belong in a judicial review. This is a policy decision. This is a budgetary decision," he said.
"This was ultimately a funding decision ... of the government."
Parrish argued that a government decision made for an improper purpose will always be under the court's purview.
Langan also said the slim stack of documents that informed the province's decision was all the government provided.

"We went to the people who decide what the budget will be, and we said, 'We need the decision on excluding Tesla vehicles,' and the documents provided are what's before you now, and you can see that there's very little there," he said.
"Sometimes there is little record."
Justice Neville reserved her decision until a later date.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Ozten Shebahkeget is a member of Northwest Angle 33 First Nation, born and raised in Winnipeg. She started writing for CBC Manitoba during the first Pathways program in 2022. She holds a master's degree in writing from the University of Saskatchewan.

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul declared a statewide disaster emergency on Monday over a measles outbreak, the first such declaration ​by a U.S. state since cases began surging in ​2025.
The state also expanded the pool of health professionals allowed to administer measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccines as cases rise in rural communities.
"No one ​should get seriously ill or die from a vaccine-preventable disease," Hochul ⁠said in a ⁠statement.

New York has reported 108 measles ‌cases this year through Oct. 3, including 92 since July 15 in under-immunized rural communities across 18 counties, well above typical annual levels, according to the executive order.

Seven of the cases are in New York ⁠City and 101 are elsewhere in the state, the governor's office said. Local health departments have administered more than 1,000 MMR doses in rural areas since July 15.
Trump signs executive order calling to reduce childhood vaccinations
Neighbouring ‌Pennsylvania is battling a fast-spreading outbreak, with 977 cases and five deaths as of Oct. 2, mostly in rural counties that border New York, the order said.
Pennsylvania health officials said on Monday the state's total had ​passed 1,000 cases, making it the largest state outbreak in more than three decades.

blocks.text: The U.S. is ⁠having its worst year for measles since 1991, with nearly 3,900 cases reported, ⁠according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

The order allows registered nurses ⁠to ⁠order tests for suspected measles and ​pharmacists to vaccinate children as young as two. It also requires all MMR vaccinations ​to be reported ⁠to state or New York City immunization registries within 72 hours, while waiving adults' consent for such reporting.
Vaccination itself still requires the consent of the patient or a legal guardian. The emergency took effect on Monday and runs through Nov. 4.

articles.title: Woman charged with murder after stabbing seven-year-old girl in Chicago
articles.summary:
Shavdon Gayden killed Eddimar Hernandez-Chacon in broad daylight while walking with her older sister

A woman has been charged with murder after allegedly stabbing a seven-year-old girl, with…

blocks.text: A woman has been charged with murder after allegedly stabbing a seven-year-old girl, with police describing it as an unprovoked attack on a sidewalk in Chicago.

Shavon Gayden, 48, has been charged with one count of first-degree murder, Chicago police said in a statement on Sunday. The killing happened just before noon on Saturday in the Chatham neighborhood. The victim has been identified by local media and the medical examiner’s office as Eddimar Hernandez-Chacon.

Police and prosecutors have said the girl was walking with her 17-year-old sister when Gayden allegedly grabbed the younger child and fatally stabbed her on a busy thoroughfare, the Chicago Tribune reported. Bystanders chased after Gayden and held her, according to police, who arrested her on the scene.

A spokesperson for the Cook county state’s attorney, which is prosecuting the case, said in an email that Gayden was supposed to appear in court on Monday, but remained hospitalized. A new hearing has been scheduled for Wednesday.
Eddimar was pronounced dead at Comer children’s hospital.
A security photo from a nearby business showed the girl walking hand in hand with an older female when she was attacked, WLS-TV reported.

It was not immediately clear if there was any relationship between the attacker and the girl. Police have not commented on a possible motive for the stabbing and declined Sunday to provide further details. The Chicago Sun-Times reported that an initial police report described the attack as “unprovoked”. The newspaper reported that Gayden’s criminal history included reports of other seemingly random attacks, including striking a Chicago Transit Authority employee – a charge for which she pleaded guilty and received two years of probation.

Attempts to reach members of Gayden’s family by phone were unsuccessful, the AP reported. Matthew Hendrickson, press secretary for the Cook county public defender, said that the office was assigned to Gayden at a hearing Monday but declined to comment further.
In a GoFundMe post to raise funds for a funeral, the girl’s uncle, Richard Hernandez Chacon, wrote that Eddimar’s “passing leaves an indescribable void and profound grief in all of us who loved her”.
The AP’s messages left with Hernandez-Chacon and another person believed to be a family member were not immediately returned.
ABC7, a local station, reported on Monday that the mother of Gayden, who requested anonymity, apologized for the stabbing and said she had struggled to get mental health treatment for her daughter.

articles.title: Coalition set to unveil dramatically deeper cuts to overseas migration as it fends off One Nation’s rise
articles.summary:
Sources say the opposition’s target will be below Labor’s but won’t match One Nation’s goal to limit net arrivals to 130,000

  • Get our

blocks.text: The Coalition is expected to reveal deep cuts to immigration today which the party says would maintain working holidaymaker places and prioritise skills as part of attempts to dent growing support for One Nation.
The opposition leader, Angus Taylor, is expected to unveil the Coalition’s policy on Tuesday, after signoff from Liberal and National MPs in a special party room meeting due to convene this morning.

Liberal sources told Guardian Australia the Coalition’s target for net overseas migration (Nom) would be significantly below Labor’s new target, but not cut as much as One Nation, which wants to limit net arrivals to 130,000 people annually, after a brief initial period of net negative migration.

The Nine newspapers reported the Coalition would initially drop net migration to around 100,000 in the first year after the election before it rose again to a figure between One Nation’s 130,000 and Labor’s target of 225,000.
As previously announced by Taylor, the number of new arrivals will be linked to housing completions in Australia.

One Nation announced last month it would cut the number of temporary migrants in Australia by more than 750,000 over three years, targeting international students and family members of skilled migrants.
The Coalition’s plan is likely to contain the largest cuts in the first year, in an effort to make an immediate impact on Nom.
Foreign students and people overstaying their visas will be part of the Coalition’s crackdown, as well as measures to remove individuals in the country without a legal pathway to stay.
Last year Australia issued more than 337,000 international student visas, of which about 45,000 went to dependants or family members of the primary applicant.
Labor’s plan, outlined by the home affairs minister, Tony Burke, will see a series of policy changes to bring Nom down to 245,000 this financial year, and 225,000 in 2027-28.
Most students will not be allowed to bring family members, and so-called visa hopping would be banned, limiting the changes students can make to their enrolment.

Nationals MPs have warned Labor’s plans to limit the number of working holidaymakers staying a second and third year in Australia would badly hurt regional industries including fruit picking, and have pushed for carve outs.
after newsletter promotion

Labor plans a ballot for backpackers wanting to stay beyond the initial first year, a measure designed to cut the number of temporary workers in the country. But regional hospitality and agriculture businesses have lobbied the Coalition to avoid cuts to its workforce.

Taylor is under pressure to stop and reverse an exodus of support to One Nation, as the party surpasses the Coalition and Labor in some opinion polls and its leader Pauline Hanson increasingly sets the terms for political and policy debate on immigration.
Liberal MP Andrew Wallace confirmed the plan had been modelled to test its effect on the Australian economy.
“You can’t just slash immigration altogether,” he told Channel Nine.
“The Coalition’s plan on migration will be very, very carefully targeted towards ensuring that we have the right number of people coming into the country, but also the right skills.
“We’ve got to ensure that our farmers and our key industries have the right skills to be able to keep the country moving, and that’s what we’ll be focused on.”
One Nation MP Barnaby Joyce, who defected from the Nationals last year, claimed credit for the Coalition plan on Tuesday.
“I congratulate the Coalition for basically coming up with our policy. There’s a bit of a nuance in there, but you know what? It shows an endorsement of where One Nation is off to,” he said.

articles.title: France braces for national day of school protests after injuries and mass arrests
articles.summary: France prepares for a day of protests in support of students who’ve been demanding more investment in education.

blocks.text: France is braced for major protests on Tuesday, after organisers called for a nationwide day of action in support of students demanding more investment in education.
It comes after a week of demonstrations, which saw students blockading hundreds of schools, at least 190 students injured, and more than 5,000 people arrested.
One student had his hand blown off during a confrontation on Monday, while another was reportedly struck in the head by a tear gas grenade last week.

France's prime minister said the government had announced measures to address their demands, but the Union Syndicale Lycéenne (USL), a major organiser of the protests, said the government had offered "nothing concrete".
The organisation called on people to join their mobilisation on Tuesday in the face of "this political deadlock and what we describe as unprecedented repression of the movement".
Some other organisations have also shown their support for the students, with the teachers' union SNES-FSU urging its members to join Tuesday's protest.

The radical-left La France Insoumise (LFI) party leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon described the protests as the "most powerful high school and university student youth movement" since 1968 - a year of major unrest, which saw millions of workers go on strike.

The wave of demonstrations began in September in Paris and has spread across the country, with students protesting over a range of issues, including overcrowded classrooms, run-down buildings, and a lack of teachers.
The protests were started by high school students, who were later joined by university students.
Last week, Eden, 14, was badly hurt in Saint-Ouen-l'Aumône after reportedly being struck on the head by a tear gas grenade.
The student suffered "a double jaw fracture" and had to undergo "extremely major surgery", according to his lawyer.
Speaking at a news conference on Monday, Eden's mother said her heart was "shattered".
"It's shameful, it's appalling, it's violent, it's horrific," French media outlet BFMTV reported her as saying.
"This should not happen. They are dealing with children who are asking for better conditions in which to study."
Among the 5,060 people arrested since the start of the movement, 87% were minors and 13% were adults, according to France's justice ministry, external.
Fourteen people have reportedly been placed in pre-trial detention, while 1,802 people are facing prosecution, including 319 adults and 1,483 minors.

The USL has accused police of using excessive force against the protesters. Responding to this allegation last week, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the demonstrations had been policed in "an extremely proportionate manner".
While France's next presidential election is still months away, the protests and the response by French authorities have been heavily politicised.
The government and hard-right politicians have blamed the hard left for fuelling the protests. Lecornu said LFI was being "irresponsible" in calling for the movement to expand.
The leader of the hard-right National Rally, Marine Le Pen, has also criticised the left for its response.

"This is no longer about high school student protests. It is about riots organised by professionals and overseen by deputies from La France Insoumise," she said, calling for a new anti-rioting law to be passed.
Meanwhile Mélenchon, the LFI's party's presidential candidate, has been blaming the police for "abuses of power", calling on people to take to the streets to "protect the youth demonstrations".

The left-wing mayor of Marseille, Benoît Payan, condemned the "unacceptable violence" in his city. While young people were "legitimately concerned" about their future and public services, they must express themselves calmly, he said.

articles.title: Pennsylvania faces largest measles outbreak in decades as case count rises to 1,000
articles.summary:
Neighboring states are also reporting hundreds of cases, with over 3,800 recorded across the country

Pennsylvania has surpassed 1,000 measles cases this year, state health officials…

blocks.text: Pennsylvania has surpassed 1,000 measles cases this year, state health officials calculate, making it the largest state outbreak in more than three decades. The benchmark comes as neighboring New York declared a state of emergency about measles rates there.
Pennsylvania’s health department said Monday 1,004 cases of measles had been confirmed. Five Pennsylvania residents ⁠have died ⁠after ​contracting the disease, with 198 hospitalizations.

Lancaster county, with sizeable Amish and Mennonite populations, remains the hardest hit, with 391 cases, according to official figures. Cases numbers have risen over the past three months, with the highest number of infections in the 24-49 age range.

The numbers, however, are not included in a CDC count due to an ongoing dispute between Pennsylvania’s governor, Josh Shapiro, and the US health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr over how to classify measles-related mortality.

Shapiro has called Kennedy “incompetent”, and Kennedy has publicly questioned whether the state’s recorded fatalities were directly caused by measles. The CDC – which Kennedy oversees – currently lists two measles deaths in the US this year.
Shapiro has expanded access to the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine in affected communities.

“I want every Pennsylvanian to know this: measles does not care about your county, your faith, or your social circle,” he said in August. “I urge everyone to take this seriously and to discuss any concerns with their trusted health care provider.”
In New York state, governor Kathy Hochul declared a state of emergency on Monday as well, citing 108 cases in the state as of 3 October.
Ohio, which also shares a border with Pennsylvania, has also reported advancing numbers of cases, with more than 200 this year. Like in Pennsylvania, Ohio has a significant Amish population.
The US is enduring its worst year for measles since 1991. As of 1 October, the CDC reported 3,887 confirmed cases this year, along with the highest number of measles-associated deaths in decades.
In addition to Pennsylvania, outbreaks have been reported in several states, including Texas and Utah, as well as South Carolina, which had the largest outbreak with 997 cases reported.
Health officials in Pennsylvania have said the state’s current outbreak started in April, west of Philadelphia and attributed the outbreak to low vaccination rates.

According to the Associated Press, the most recent outbreak to surpass 1,000 cases occurred in New York City in the early 1990s. That outbreak infected more than 4,500 people. During the 1989 and 1991 resurgences, 55,000 infections and 123 deaths ⁠were recorded, according to Reuters.
The domestic US spread of measles was eliminated in 2000 by high vaccination rates, but those rates have fallen in recent years to below the 95% coverage needed to prevent outbreaks.
In November, international health officials will meet to determine if the US and Mexico have lost their measles-free status.

articles.title: ICC unseals Taliban leaders' warrants over persecuting women
articles.summary: The court gave more details on the warrants for four Taliban leaders accused of the crime against humanity of gender persecution of women, girls and the LGBTQ+ community. The Islamist group rejected…

image.caption: The Taliban has significantly restricted several rights of women and girls since taking power [FILE: May 23, 2023]Image: Ebrahim Noroozi/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The International Criminal Court (ICC) disclosed on Monday more details about the arrest warrants against two Taliban leaders, while also issuing two more arrest warrants.
The four Taliban leaders are accused of crimes against humanity through the persecution of women, girls and the LGBTQ+ community in Afghanistan since taking power in 2021.

According to the court, warrants were issued in July and September of last year against Hibatullah Akhundzada , the Taliban's Supreme Leader, as well as against Abdul Hakim Haqqani, who heads the country's Supreme Court.
The other two warrants were issued against Education Minister Habibullah Agha and Minister of Higher Education Neda Mohammad Nadim.

The four are charged with persecution on grounds of gender of "girls, women and other persons nonconforming with the Taliban's policy on gender, gender identity or expression; and on political grounds against persons perceived as 'allies of girls and women,'" according to the court.

blocks.caption: An arrest warrant was issued against Taliban Supreme Leader Hibatullah Akhundzada [FILE: Aug 14, 2023]Image: WAKIL KOHSAR/AFP

blocks.text: What does the ICC accuse the 4 Taliban leaders of?

The judges who issued the warrants said that the four implemented policies that saw "severe violations of fundamental rights and freedoms of the civilian population of Afghanistan, in connection with conducts of murder, imprisonment, torture, rape and enforced disappearance."

The Taliban "specifically targeted girls and women by reason of their gender," the judges added, also mentioning persecution against people due to "certain expressions of sexuality and/or gender identity."
The ICC has no jurisdiction to execute the warrants. Still, the move is considered a form of pressure on the Afghan ruling authority.
The Taliban have taken a wide range of measures to restrict women's access to jobs and education beyond sixth grade, as well as barring them from most public spaces.
Women are also obligated to cover their whole bodies apart from their eyes upon leaving home, with a male relative having to accompany them on long trips.
Taliban rejects ICC's warrants
Afghanistan's government spokesperson said the country does not recognize the court's authority.
"We are bound by the rulings of Islamic Sharia and its courts, not by intelligence entities or so-called courts." chief spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid said in a statement.

blocks.caption: The Taliban has returned to rule over Afghanistan since August 2021Image: Javid Ashna/Middle East Images/picture alliance

blocks.text: A request for warrants for Akhundzada and Haqqani made last year by former ICC chief prosecutor Karim Khan argued that "Afghan women and girls as well as the LGBTQI+ community are facing an unprecedented, unconscionable and ongoing persecution by the Taliban.”
The UN Human Rights Council has called on the Taliban to drop its "systematic oppression of all women and girls in Afghanistan."
Human rights groups have been calling for the international community to do more against the Taliban's gender-based policies in Afghanistan.
In Afghanistan, girls study in secret to skirt Taliban ban

articles.title: Conservatives propose £10bn ‘Britannia Shield’ inspired by Israel’s Iron Dome
articles.summary:
Party to unveil plans for one of UK’s ‘most significant military programmes since the cold war’

The Conservatives will announce plans to build a £10bn British “Iron Dome” similar to…

blocks.text: The Conservatives will announce plans to build a £10bn British “Iron Dome” similar to Israel’s air and missile defence system, which the party will christen “Britannia Shield” in an announcement at conference on Tuesday.

The shadow defence secretary, James Cartlidge, will say Britain needs to be ready to defend itself from potential aerial attacks and that new investment was needed in advanced radar and interceptor missiles.
Claiming it was “one of Britain’s most significant military programmes since the cold war”, he will say it is one that was “totally necessary because of the threats we face”.

Britain’s military has traditionally believed it does not need to purchase Iron Dome-style air defence systems given other spending priorities and the fact that the UK has not faced drone and missile strikes as has Israel or Ukraine.

Military officials argue that the UK’s strategy is based around deterring any attack or a full-blown war with nuclear weapons and that any conflict that involved a direct threat to the British homeland would almost certainly involve Nato allies assisting.

The UK does not own any Patriot air defence systems, and in an acute crisis would have to rely on Royal Navy Type 45 destroyers to protect coastal areas, but the circumstances in which expensive air defence would be needed in the UK are very remote.
The Conservatives will say the new system would be funded out of the defence uplift from their commitment last month to increase defence spending by more than £10bn a year to reach 3% of GDP by 2030.

Cartlidge will say in his speech that the aim would be to deliver a minimum deployable capability within the first five years, with further improvements, expanded capability and missile stockpiles delivered over the following five years.

The party will argue that the UK is being left behind in Europe when it comes to investment in air defences, which was criticised in a report from the defence select committee last November. The government has currently committed about £790m for integrated air and missile defence (IAMD) in the Defence Investment Plan.

Cartlidge will say that the British version of the Iron Dome will have new advanced radar systems to detect threats, a new command and control system and a new stockpile of missiles and counter-drone capabilities.

That would in practice be a fundamentally different model to the Israeli Iron Dome system, which protects a country a twelfth of the size of Great Britain and is primarily designed to counter short-range threats like rockets and artillery, with other defence systems that counter longer-range missiles.

Other European countries, including Germany, Greece, Cyprus and Poland, are investing significantly in air defence systems, though the UK is under limited direct threat from ongoing conflicts, unlike some of those nations.

The Conservative leader, Kemi Badenoch, said that Labour were “failing that basic test” of keeping the country safe. The chancellor, John Healey – who previously quit as Keir Starmer’s defence secretary over the limitations of his defence settlement – is now unlikely to set out when the UK will meet the target of spending 3% of GDP on defence until next year’s spending review.

“The world will not wait for Britain to get ready. War has returned to Europe. Missiles and drones are transforming warfare in the Middle East. Cheap weapons can now threaten cities, military bases and critical infrastructure in ways that would have sounded like science fiction a generation ago,” Badenoch said, announcing the air defence investment.

“If a missile or drone is launched at Britain, we do not get a second chance to wish we had prepared. Families can make their own choices. Businesses can build and innovate. But only government can defend the country.”
